A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSFT work. The complete main text and Appendices A.1–A.5 are readable, including all three tables, eleven figures, algorithms, and equations. Reformatting from 20 to 22 pages does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SSFT experiments with 32B and 7B models, benchmark accuracies, matching analyses, training dynamics, and generated reasoning examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, matching analyses, training dynamics, and reasoning examples in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The matching procedure, full-trace training loss, inference token selection, and distributed batching remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2. Revised loss terminology and optional filtering descriptions clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same s1k mixed-teacher and fixed-teacher training data and the 93k-question Open-R1 subset. Evaluation still covers AIME 2024, AIME 2025, MATH-500, and GPQA-Diamond.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, including s1.1-32B, Multiverse-32B, the OSS and mixed-distillation SFT baselines, random-matching SSFT, and the 7B comparisons. Figure 4 retains the same temperature-scaled comparators. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1 and A.3 retain the same model configurations, training budgets, generation settings, and matching-token limits. Renaming Pass@1 of Native Cons@6 to Average of Native Cons@6 clarifies the label; the six-generation majority-vote calculation is unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the temperature comparison, random versus optimal matching analyses, four versus six reserved-token study, and Open-R1 ablation. Appendix training-dynamics analyses and all six AIME reasoning examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report averaging Pass@1 over 32 generations and Cons@6 over 11 generation sets. Figures 5–6 retain the same per-token averaging descriptions. No seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical entries; for example, SSFT-32B's Table 1 averages remain 68.15, 77.23, and 82.11. The plotted results in Figures 4–10 and the qualitative reasoning examples in Appendix A.4 also match.

T1.justification: The matching definitions, assumptions, and Equations 1–10 are unchanged. Additional explanations distinguish matching costs from the Hungarian training loss without introducing new mathematical reasoning, proofs, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about learning global forking tokens, preserving diverse reasoning modes, and improving performance over SFT. The introduction rephrases the implementation contribution and diversity claims without establishing a new capability or scientific guarantee.

C2.justification: Figure 1 and Section 3.3 explain emergence through cross-question specialization without explicit consistency regularization and add that relative reasoning lengths may vary by question. Section 4 strengthens its warning about Parallel-R1 from possible similar traces to asserting that set loss is necessary to prevent diversity collapse.

D1.justification: v2 supplies concrete code and collection references on its first page, replacing v1's forthcoming-release statements, and identifies the implementation's HuggingFace basis. Appendix hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and implementation algorithms remain unchanged. The PDFs establish improved access documentation, not verification of the linked resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds Haozhe Wang et al. on emergent hierarchical reasoning, Yu et al.'s Chain-of-Reasoning, and Zheng et al.'s mixture-of-thought work. Section 4 briefly connects SSFT to predefined reasoning paradigms and revises its discussion of Parallel-R1; the broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the implementation contribution and emergence explanation, clarify loss and metric terminology, update affiliations, and add an acknowledgment. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain the same; this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document-wide template, narrowing the text block, adding a running header, redesigning the title area, and extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figures 5–6 now share a page, while Algorithm 2 and Figure 11 occupy separate pages. Figure 2 also gains optimization-variable labels. The underlying scientific graphics are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer loss terminology and the revised Cons@6 label, added research context, and concrete code/collection references modestly improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. Smaller displays and additional breaks within appendix examples reduce convenience, while the stronger necessity assertion receives no new support; these tradeoffs limit the overall gain.
